question: Why is my laptop running so slow and how can I speed it up?
alternatives: My computer is lagging badly, what can I do?
How to fix a slow laptop?
PC running very slow and freezing
Why is my laptop taking forever to respond?
answer: A slow computer is usually caused by excessive startup applications, low storage space, overheating, or background resource hogs. To speed it up: 1) Open Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) and check CPU/RAM usage; 2) Disable unneeded startup programs in the 'Startup' tab; 3) Free up disk space by removing temporary files or running Disk Cleanup; 4) Check for malware scans; and 5) Ensure cooling vents are dust-free to prevent thermal throttling.

question: What should I do if my laptop won't turn on or charge?
alternatives: Laptop won't power on at all
Computer not turning on and screen is black
Laptop battery not charging when plugged in
My laptop is completely dead
answer: If your laptop doesn't power on: 1) Check the power adapter connection and verify the charging indicator LED is lit; 2) Test with a different wall outlet; 3) Perform a hard power reset by disconnecting the charger, holding down the power button for 30 seconds, reconnecting the charger, and turning it back on; 4) Inspect the charging port and cable for physical damage. If the battery is swollen or failing, seek certified hardware repair.

question: Why does my laptop fan make loud noises and get extremely hot?
alternatives: Laptop overheating and fan running at full speed
Noisy fan on my computer
Computer feels very hot to the touch
Why is my PC fan loud and buzzing?
laptop bahut garam ho raha hai
laptop getting heated up very quickly
answer: Loud fan noise and overheating occur when dust obstructs airflow or demanding processes stress the CPU/GPU. Steps to fix: 1) Place the laptop on a hard, flat surface rather than beds or pillows; 2) Clean exhaust vents using compressed air (in short bursts while powered off); 3) Open Task Manager to terminate runaway background tasks; 4) Update BIOS and chipset drivers to ensure proper fan curve management.

question: How do I fix a blue screen of death (BSOD) crash?
alternatives: Computer keeps getting Blue Screen BSOD
Windows crashed with a blue screen error
PC reboots randomly with blue screen error code
How to troubleshoot BSOD on Windows?
answer: A Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) indicates a critical hardware or kernel driver failure. To resolve it: 1) Note the stop code (e.g., IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, MEMORY_MANAGEMENT); 2) Restart into Safe Mode if Windows won't boot normally; 3) Run 'sfc /scannow' and 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' in an Administrator Command Prompt; 4) Update graphics and motherboard drivers; 5) Test RAM integrity using Windows Memory Diagnostic (mdsched.exe).

question: Why is my laptop keyboard or touchpad not responding?
alternatives: Trackpad stopped working on my laptop
Keys not typing on keyboard
Mouse cursor won't move using touchpad
Laptop keyboard frozen
answer: If the built-in keyboard or touchpad stops working: 1) Check if the touchpad was accidentally disabled via function keys (e.g., Fn + F7 or F9 depending on laptop brand); 2) Connect an external USB mouse or keyboard to verify OS responsiveness; 3) Open Device Manager (Win + X > Device Manager), expand 'Keyboards' and 'Mice', right-click the device, and select 'Update driver' or 'Uninstall device', then reboot; 4) Run the Windows Keyboard troubleshooter in Settings.

question: How do I connect an external monitor or dual displays to my computer?
alternatives: External display not detected on laptop
How to set up second monitor in Windows?
Dual screen setup not showing picture
Second monitor says no signal
answer: To set up an external monitor: 1) Connect the HDMI, DisplayPort, or USB-C cable securely between the computer and monitor; 2) Ensure the monitor is powered on and set to the correct input source; 3) Press Win + P on your keyboard to choose 'Duplicate' or 'Extend'; 4) If no signal is received, go to Settings > System > Display > Multiple displays and click 'Detect'; 5) Update your graphics card drivers.

question: Why is my computer speaker producing no sound or crackling audio?
alternatives: No sound on my computer
Audio not working on laptop speakers or headphones
Sound is crackling or distorted on PC
How to fix audio problems in Windows?
answer: To restore sound: 1) Check the taskbar speaker icon to ensure volume is not muted or set to zero; 2) Click the sound icon and verify the correct output device (e.g., Realtek Speakers vs HDMI/Headphones) is selected; 3) Run the Windows Audio Troubleshooter (Settings > System > Sound > Troubleshoot); 4) Reinstall or update the audio driver in Device Manager under 'Sound, video and game controllers'; 5) Disable audio enhancements in Sound Settings if experiencing crackling.

question: How do I fix a software installation that keeps failing or freezing?
alternatives: Program won't install on Windows
Installer freezes during installation
Software setup failed error
Why can't I install an application on my PC?
answer: If software installation fails: 1) Right-click the installer executable and choose 'Run as administrator'; 2) Verify sufficient free storage space exists on the installation drive; 3) Check that your OS meets the program's minimum system requirements (e.g., 64-bit architecture, specific runtime libraries like .NET or Visual C++ Redistributable); 4) Temporarily pause third-party antivirus that may falsely block setup files; 5) Re-download the setup installer in case of corruption.

question: How do I completely uninstall an application and remove its leftover files?
alternatives: How to cleanly remove software from PC?
Uninstall program that won't go away
How do I uninstall an app in Windows 11/10?
Delete software remnants and leftover registry files
answer: To uninstall an application: 1) Go to Settings > Apps > Installed apps (or Control Panel > Programs and Features); 2) Locate the software, click the three dots, and choose 'Uninstall'; 3) Follow the wizard; 4) To remove leftover cache and config folders, check '%AppData%' and '%LocalAppData%' via the Run dialog (Win + R) and delete the folder associated with the removed vendor; 5) Restart your computer.

question: How do I fix Windows Update when it gets stuck downloading or installing?
alternatives: Windows update stuck at 0% or failing with error code
Updates won't install on Windows
Windows update loop or frozen
How to reset Windows Update components?
answer: If Windows Update is stuck: 1) Run the built-in troubleshooter at Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update; 2) Restart the Windows Update service: Open Command Prompt as Admin and run 'net stop wuauserv', 'net stop bits', then delete files in 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution', and restart services with 'net start wuauserv' and 'net start bits'; 3) Ensure at least 15-20 GB of free disk space is available.

question: Why won't an older software program run on modern Windows 10 or 11?
alternatives: Old program not compatible with Windows 11
How to run legacy software on modern Windows?
Software compatibility issue with new OS
How to use Windows Compatibility Mode?
answer: To run older software on modern Windows: 1) Right-click the application's executable or shortcut and select 'Properties'; 2) Switch to the 'Compatibility' tab; 3) Check 'Run this program in compatibility mode for' and pick Windows 7 or Windows XP; 4) Check 'Run this program as an administrator'; 5) Click 'Change high DPI settings' if UI fonts appear blurry; 6) Click Apply and launch the application.

question: What should I do if an application crashes immediately upon opening?
alternatives: App closes immediately after launching
Program crashes on startup
Software opens and shuts down right away
Application stopped working as soon as opened
answer: When an app crashes on startup: 1) Check Windows Event Viewer (Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Application) to see the crash fault module or exception code; 2) Update your graphics card drivers and reinstall Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable packages (both x86 and x64); 3) Try running the application as Administrator; 4) Delete the application's local user configuration cache in %AppData%; 5) Reinstall the application.

question: How do I safely install Python and verify pip works on Windows?
alternatives: How to set up Python on Windows?
pip is not recognized as an internal or external command
How to install Python and add to PATH?
Python environment setup troubleshooting
answer: To install Python properly on Windows: 1) Download the official installer from python.org; 2) Crucial step: on the initial install screen, check the box 'Add python.exe to PATH'; 3) Select Customize installation and ensure pip and IDLE are checked; 4) Complete the setup and click 'Disable path length limit'; 5) Open a new PowerShell terminal and verify by running 'python --version' and 'pip --version'.

question: How do I stop apps from opening automatically when my computer boots?
alternatives: Disable startup programs in Windows
Too many apps launching when PC starts
How to turn off startup apps?
Stop software from opening on startup
answer: To disable startup apps: 1) Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager; 2) Click on the 'Startup apps' tab (speedometer or list icon); 3) Review the 'Startup impact' column; 4) Right-click any non-essential application (such as Spotify, Discord, or Steam) and select 'Disable'; 5) Alternatively, manage them in Windows Settings > Apps > Startup.

question: Why does my Wi-Fi say 'Connected, no internet access'?
alternatives: Connected to Wi-Fi but websites won't load
No internet access on wireless network
Wi-Fi icon has an exclamation point or globe icon
How to fix Connected No Internet error?
wifi connect nahi ho raha
internet nahi chal raha
answer: The 'Connected, no internet' status means your device is linked to the router, but the router cannot communicate with your Internet Service Provider. To fix: 1) Restart both your modem and Wi-Fi router by unplugging them for 30 seconds; 2) Disconnect and reconnect to the Wi-Fi network; 3) Open Command Prompt as Administrator and flush DNS by typing 'ipconfig /flushdns', followed by 'netsh winsock reset'; 4) Restart your computer.

question: How do I fix slow internet and high ping latency?
alternatives: Internet speed is very slow
High ping and lag on my Wi-Fi
Why is my download speed so slow?
How to boost Wi-Fi speed at home?
answer: To address slow internet speeds: 1) Connect to the 5 GHz Wi-Fi band instead of 2.4 GHz for higher throughput; 2) Position your computer closer to the router or use an Ethernet cable for a direct connection; 3) Check for background cloud syncs or game updates consuming bandwidth; 4) Reboot the router; 5) Run a speed test at speedtest.net to verify whether speeds match your ISP subscription plan.

question: What should I do if my Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting and reconnecting?
alternatives: Wireless network drops connection randomly
Wi-Fi keeps dropping every few minutes
Unstable Wi-Fi connection on laptop
Why does my computer keep disconnecting from Wi-Fi?
answer: If Wi-Fi repeatedly drops: 1) Go to Device Manager > Network adapters, right-click your Wi-Fi card > Properties > Power Management tab, and uncheck 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'; 2) Update your Wi-Fi adapter drivers from the manufacturer's website (Intel, Realtek, or Qualcomm); 3) Forget the Wi-Fi network and reconnect with the password; 4) Change your router's wireless channel in router settings to reduce local radio interference.

question: How do I change DNS servers to Google DNS or Cloudflare for faster browsing?
alternatives: How to configure DNS in Windows?
Switch to Cloudflare DNS 1.1.1.1 or Google 8.8.8.8
Fix DNS probe finished nxdomain error
Change DNS settings on computer
answer: To change DNS servers in Windows: 1) Go to Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi (or Ethernet); 2) Click 'Hardware properties'; 3) Beside 'DNS server assignment', click 'Edit' and select 'Manual'; 4) Toggle on IPv4; 5) For Cloudflare, enter Preferred: 1.1.1.1, Alternate: 1.0.0.1; for Google DNS, enter Preferred: 8.8.8.8, Alternate: 8.8.4.4; 6) Save settings and flush DNS by running 'ipconfig /flushdns' in Command Prompt.

question: Why is my Wi-Fi adapter missing or not showing up in Windows?
alternatives: Wi-Fi icon disappeared completely
No Wi-Fi option in settings or taskbar
Wireless adapter not found in Device Manager
Can't turn on Wi-Fi
answer: When the Wi-Fi adapter option disappears: 1) Perform a cold restart (shut down completely, unplug power for 60 seconds, turn back on); 2) Open Device Manager, click Action > 'Scan for hardware changes'; 3) Look under Network adapters for warning triangles; right-click and select 'Enable device'; 4) If listed as an unknown device, download the official Wi-Fi driver on a phone or other PC, transfer via USB, and install it; 5) Check physical wireless toggle switch on laptop if present.

question: How do I find my computer's local IP address and default gateway?
alternatives: How to check my IP address in Windows?
Find router default gateway IP
What is my local IP address?
Where to find IPv4 address in Command Prompt?
answer: To find your network IP details: 1) Press Win + R, type 'cmd', and press Enter; 2) Type 'ipconfig' and press Enter; 3) Look under your active network adapter (Wi-Fi or Ethernet) for: 'IPv4 Address' (your computer's local IP, typically 192.168.x.x or 10.x.x.x) and 'Default Gateway' (your router's administrative IP address).

question: How do I test network connectivity and packet loss using ping and traceroute?
alternatives: How to run a ping test?
Diagnose packet loss in Windows cmd
How to use tracert to diagnose network issues?
Test internet connection stability
answer: To test connectivity: 1) Open Command Prompt; 2) Type 'ping 8.8.8.8 -n 10' to send 10 packets to Google DNS. Check the 'Lost' count (packet loss should be 0%) and latency average; 3) Type 'ping google.com' to test DNS resolution; 4) Type 'tracert google.com' to trace each network hop between your machine and the destination server, helping identify where latency or timeout drops happen.

question: What should I do if I forgot my Windows login password or PIN?
alternatives: Locked out of Windows account
Forgot my computer password how to reset?
Can't sign in to Windows PIN not working
Reset Windows login credentials
answer: If locked out of Windows: 1) For Microsoft Accounts, click 'I forgot my PIN/password' on the login screen or reset it from another device at account.live.com/password/reset; 2) For local accounts with security questions set, enter an incorrect password, click 'Reset password', and answer your security prompts; 3) If you have a second Administrator account on the PC, sign into it to reset the password for the locked user account.

question: How do I set up two-factor authentication (2FA) to secure my accounts?
alternatives: How to enable 2FA / MFA on my online accounts?
What is two-step verification and how to use it?
Best way to secure accounts with authenticator app
Enable multi factor authentication
answer: To set up Two-Factor Authentication (2FA): 1) Download an authenticator app (such as Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or Aegis) on your smartphone; 2) In your online account (Google, GitHub, banking), go to Security Settings > 2-Step Verification; 3) Choose 'Authenticator App' and scan the QR code displayed on screen; 4) Enter the 6-digit confirmation code generated by the app; 5) Save your backup recovery codes securely in an offline location.

question: What is the best way to create and manage strong passwords safely?
alternatives: How to create an unhackable strong password?
Should I use a password manager?
Best practices for password security
How to stop forgetting complicated passwords?
answer: Best practices for passwords: 1) Use a passphrase of 4-5 random words (e.g., 'cactus-ocean-battery-staple') or a 16+ character string with mixed case, numbers, and symbols; 2) Never reuse passwords across accounts; 3) Use a reputable password manager (such as Bitwarden, 1Password, or KeePass) to generate and store credentials encrypted; 4) Enable biometrics or a strong master password on your vault.

question: What steps should I take if I suspect my email or online account was hacked?
alternatives: My email was compromised, what do I do?
Someone hacked my account
Suspicious activity on my Google account
How to recover a hacked account?
answer: If your account was compromised: 1) Immediately attempt to change the password from a secure device; 2) Go to account security settings and select 'Sign out of all sessions/devices'; 3) Review linked recovery email addresses and phone numbers to ensure attackers didn't alter them; 4) Enable 2FA immediately; 5) Check for unauthorized email forwarding rules or filters; 6) Notify affected contacts if spam was sent from your address.

question: How do I switch from a Microsoft Account to a Local Account in Windows?
alternatives: Use local account instead of Microsoft account on Windows
How to unlink Microsoft account from PC?
Convert Windows user to local offline account
Sign in with local account Windows 11
answer: To switch to a local account: 1) Open Settings > Accounts > Your info; 2) Look for the link 'Sign in with a local account instead' (under Account settings); 3) Confirm your current Microsoft account password; 4) Choose your new local username, set a password and password hint; 5) Click 'Sign out and finish' to complete the transition.

question: How do I create a new user profile with Administrator rights in Windows?
alternatives: Add new admin account on Windows PC
Create another user account Windows 10/11
How to grant administrator privileges to user?
Make user account an admin
answer: To create a new Admin account: 1) Go to Settings > Accounts > Other users; 2) Click 'Add account'; 3) Choose 'I don't have this person's sign-in information' > 'Add a user without a Microsoft account'; 4) Enter a username and password; 5) Once created, select the new account, click 'Change account type', and change it from 'Standard User' to 'Administrator'.

question: How do I clear saved passwords and autofill data from my web browser?
alternatives: Remove saved passwords from Chrome or Edge
How to delete autofill login credentials in browser?
Clear stored website passwords
Delete password history in browser
answer: To remove saved passwords: 1) In Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge, press Ctrl + Shift + Delete; 2) Switch to the 'Advanced' tab; 3) Set time range to 'All time'; 4) Check 'Passwords and other sign-in data' and 'Autofill form data'; 5) Click 'Clear data'. You can also view and selectively delete individual saved entries in chrome://password-manager/passwords or edge://wallet/passwords.

question: What is the 3-2-1 backup strategy and how do I implement it?
alternatives: Best way to back up my computer files
Explain the 3 2 1 backup rule
How should I protect my data from loss?
Safe backup strategy for personal files
answer: The 3-2-1 backup rule states: 1) Keep 3 copies of your data (1 primary copy and 2 backups); 2) Store them on 2 different types of storage media (e.g., your computer's internal SSD and an external USB hard drive); 3) Keep 1 copy off-site (such as a secure cloud backup service like OneDrive, Google Drive, or Backblaze) to protect against physical disaster, theft, or ransomware.

question: How do I recover an accidentally deleted file on Windows?
alternatives: How to restore deleted files?
Accidentally emptied Recycle Bin how to recover?
Retrieve deleted document in Windows
Can I get back a permanently deleted file?
answer: To recover deleted files: 1) First check the Recycle Bin on your desktop, right-click the file and click 'Restore'; 2) If emptied, check OneDrive or cloud version history; 3) Right-click the folder where the file used to reside, choose Properties > 'Previous Versions' tab to restore a shadow copy; 4) Use Microsoft's official free tool 'Windows File Recovery' from the Microsoft Store, or reputable software like Recuva; 5) Stop writing new data to the drive immediately to prevent overwriting.

question: How do I safely free up disk space on my C drive when it is full?
alternatives: C drive is red and out of space
How to clean up disk space on Windows?
Computer low on storage space
Free up space on hard drive
answer: To free up C drive space safely: 1) Open Settings > System > Storage and enable 'Storage Sense'; 2) Click 'Temporary files' and remove previous Windows installations, temporary setup files, and downloads; 3) Run 'cleanmgr' (Disk Cleanup) as Administrator and select system files; 4) Move large personal video, photo, or game libraries to a secondary drive; 5) Use free analysis tools like TreeSize Free or WizTree to identify hidden bulky folders.

question: How do I zip and unzip compressed folders on Windows without extra software?
alternatives: How to extract a zip file on Windows?
Create a zip archive folder in Windows
Uncompress zip file without WinRAR
How to open .zip files?
answer: Windows natively supports ZIP files: 1) To compress: select the files or folders, right-click, and select 'Compress to ZIP file' (or Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder); 2) To extract: right-click the .zip archive, select 'Extract All...', choose the destination folder, and click 'Extract'. No third-party tools like WinRAR or 7-Zip are required for standard .zip files.

question: How do I fix the 'File is open in another program' error when deleting?
alternatives: Can't delete file because it is in use
File in use error Windows cannot delete
Force delete locked file in Windows
The action can't be completed because the file is open
answer: To delete a locked file: 1) Ensure the application that opened it is closed; 2) Open Task Manager, locate any background process associated with the file (e.g., Word, Adobe Acrobat, Python), and end task; 3) If the locking process is unknown, use Microsoft PowerToys 'File Locksmith' utility or Sysinternals Process Explorer to identify the handle; 4) Alternatively, restart your PC in Safe Mode and delete the file.

question: How do I configure File History for automated local backups in Windows?
alternatives: How to use Windows File History?
Set up automatic backup to external hard drive
Back up Documents and Pictures automatically in Windows
File History configuration guide
answer: To set up File History: 1) Connect an external hard drive; 2) Go to Control Panel > System and Security > File History; 3) Select your external drive as the backup target; 4) Click 'Turn on'; 5) Use 'Advanced settings' to choose backup frequency (e.g., hourly or daily) and version retention period. Windows will now automatically preserve versioned snapshots of your user libraries.

question: How do I safely format a USB flash drive or external drive?
alternatives: Format USB drive in Windows
Which file system should I format USB: NTFS, FAT32, or exFAT?
Wipe flash drive and change format
How to format thumb drive?
answer: To format a USB drive: 1) Back up any valuable files, as formatting erases all data; 2) Open File Explorer > This PC, right-click the USB drive and select 'Format...'; 3) Choose the File System: 'exFAT' for universal compatibility between Windows and macOS with files >4GB, 'FAT32' for legacy compatibility (4GB file size limit), or 'NTFS' for Windows-only drives; 4) Check 'Quick Format' and click Start.

question: How do I boot Windows into Safe Mode to troubleshoot problems?
alternatives: How to enter Safe Mode in Windows 10/11?
Boot into safe mode when PC won't start normally
Access Windows Safe Mode troubleshooting
How to restart in safe mode?
answer: To enter Safe Mode: 1) Hold the Shift key while clicking Restart on the Start Menu or login screen; 2) Your PC will reboot to the 'Choose an option' screen; 3) Navigate to Troubleshoot > Advanced options > Startup Settings > click Restart; 4) When the numbered list appears, press '4' for Safe Mode or '5' for Safe Mode with Networking.

question: How do I use System File Checker (SFC) and DISM to repair corrupt Windows files?
alternatives: Run sfc scannow to fix corrupted Windows files
How to repair Windows image using DISM?
Fix corrupted system files in Windows cmd
How to use SFC and DISM commands?
answer: To repair system file corruption: 1) Press Win + X and select 'Terminal (Admin)' or 'Command Prompt (Admin)'; 2) First run the DISM repair command: 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' and wait for it to complete; 3) Then run the System File Checker command: 'sfc /scannow'; 4) Wait until verification reaches 100%. If corrupted files were found and repaired, restart your computer.

question: How do I use System Restore to roll back Windows to an earlier working state?
alternatives: How to restore PC to earlier date with System Restore?
Roll back Windows update or bad driver
Use System Restore point in Windows
Undo recent system changes Windows
answer: To use System Restore: 1) Press Win + R, type 'rstrui.exe', and press Enter; 2) The System Restore wizard will open; click 'Next'; 3) Select a restore point created prior to when your issue started (check 'Show more restore points' if available); 4) Click 'Scan for affected programs' to see which updates or apps will be removed; 5) Click Finish. Note: personal files and documents will not be affected.

question: Why is my Windows search bar or Start menu freezing or not working?
alternatives: Start menu won't open in Windows 11/10
Search bar not typing or responding in taskbar
Windows search indexed stopped working
How to fix broken Start menu?
answer: If the Start Menu or Search bar freezes: 1) Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager, locate 'Windows Explorer' under Processes, right-click and click 'Restart'; 2) Open Task Manager > Services tab, find 'WSearch', right-click and restart it; 3) Run the Search troubleshooter in Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Search and Indexing; 4) As a last resort, re-register Start Menu components via PowerShell.

question: How do I enable or disable dark mode in Windows 10 and 11?
alternatives: Switch Windows to dark theme
Turn on dark mode in Windows settings
Change light mode to dark mode PC
How to enable dark theme?
answer: To enable Dark Mode: 1) Press Win + I to open Settings; 2) Navigate to 'Personalization' in the left menu; 3) Click on 'Colors'; 4) Under 'Choose your mode', click the dropdown and choose 'Dark' (or choose 'Custom' to set Windows UI to dark while keeping apps light); 5) Your taskbar, Start menu, File Explorer, and native apps will immediately apply dark theme.

question: What should I do if Windows says 'Disk 100% usage' in Task Manager?
alternatives: Task manager shows 100 percent disk usage
Hard drive pegged at 100% and lagging
Why is my disk usage always 100% in Windows?
Fix 100% disk usage bug
answer: To fix 100% disk usage: 1) Identify the consuming process in Task Manager sorted by the Disk column; 2) Temporarily disable Windows Search service to test if indexing is stuck (run 'net.exe stop "Windows Search"' in admin cmd); 3) Disable SysMain service ('net.exe stop sysmain') which frequently causes high disk I/O on mechanical HDDs; 4) Run 'chkdsk C: /f /r' to check for physical drive bad sectors; 5) Upgrade mechanical hard drives (HDD) to a modern SSD for permanent relief.

question: How do I perform a clean 'Reset this PC' without losing personal files?
alternatives: Reset Windows without losing files
How to factory reset Windows while keeping my files?
Reset this PC keep files option
Reinstall Windows without data loss
Factory reset Windows 10/11
answer: To reset Windows while keeping personal files: 1) Go to Settings > System > Recovery; 2) Beside 'Reset this PC', click 'Reset PC'; 3) Choose 'Keep my files' (this removes apps and settings, but preserves personal documents and media); 4) Choose 'Cloud download' for a fresh Windows image or 'Local reinstall'; 5) Follow the prompt and confirm. Note: always maintain an external backup as best practice before running any OS reset.

question: How do I fix 'MSVCP140.dll or VCRUNTIME140.dll is missing' error?
alternatives: VCRUNTIME140.dll not found error
Missing DLL error when launching game or app
How to fix MSVCP140.dll was not found?
Program can't start because dll is missing
answer: This error occurs when the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable runtime required by the application is not installed. To fix: 1) Go to Microsoft's official website and download the 'Visual C++ Redistributable for Visual Studio 2015-2022'; 2) Important: Install BOTH the x86 (vc_redist.x86.exe) and x64 (vc_redist.x64.exe) packages on 64-bit Windows; 3) Restart your PC; 4) Avoid downloading standalone DLL files from unofficial third-party websites, as they often contain malware.

question: How do I force quit a frozen program that won't close?
alternatives: App is not responding how to force close?
Program frozen can't close window
Kill stuck process in Windows
How to force close an app without restarting?
answer: To force close a frozen program: 1) Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager; 2) Locate the unresponsive app under the 'Processes' tab; 3) Click the app and click the 'End task' button in the upper right; 4) Alternatively, press Alt + F4 while the frozen window is focused; 5) For persistent stubborn tasks, open Command Prompt and run 'taskkill /f /im <app_name>.exe' (e.g. taskkill /f /im chrome.exe).

question: Why does Google Chrome or Edge keep showing 'Aw, Snap!' or 'STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION'?
alternatives: Web browser tabs crashing constantly
Chrome Aw Snap error code
STATUS ACCESS VIOLATION in Edge or Chrome
Browser page crashes every time I load website
answer: To fix browser tab crashes: 1) Disable browser extensions one by one (chrome://extensions or edge://extensions), especially ad-blockers or script injectors, to identify the culprit; 2) Clear cache and cookies via Ctrl + Shift + Delete; 3) Turn off hardware acceleration in Settings > System > 'Use graphics acceleration when available'; 4) Update your browser to the latest version; 5) Check for faulty RAM with Windows Memory Diagnostic.

question: How do I fix Microsoft Office or Word 'Unlicensed Product' or activation errors?
alternatives: Word says Unlicensed Product
Microsoft 365 activation error
Excel unlicensed product warning banner
How to fix Office activation problems?
answer: To resolve Office activation errors: 1) Verify you are signed into Office with the exact email address associated with your subscription (File > Account); 2) Check your computer's date, time, and time zone in Windows Settings (inaccurate clocks prevent SSL license verification); 3) Run Office as Administrator and click 'Update Options > Update Now'; 4) Run the Microsoft Support and Recovery Assistant (SaRA) tool from Microsoft.

question: Why is my Zoom or Teams webcam not working or showing a black screen?
alternatives: Webcam black screen in Teams or Zoom
Camera not detected on video call
Zoom camera not working on laptop
Fix webcam permissions in Windows
answer: To fix webcam issues: 1) Check if your laptop has a physical privacy slider over the camera lens or a dedicated camera toggle key (e.g., F10 or Fn + key); 2) Check Windows privacy permissions: Settings > Privacy & security > Camera, and ensure 'Camera access' and 'Let apps access your camera' are turned ON; 3) In Zoom/Teams settings, confirm the correct camera device is chosen; 4) Close other apps that might be using the camera.

question: How do I resolve the 0xc000007b application error when starting a game or software?
alternatives: The application was unable to start correctly 0xc000007b
Fix error 0xc000007b in Windows
Game won't launch 0xc000007b
Application startup error 0xc000007b
answer: Error 0xc000007b indicates a 32-bit and 64-bit architecture conflict, typically between the application and DirectX or Visual C++ runtime modules. To fix: 1) Reinstall Microsoft DirectX End-User Runtimes; 2) Reinstall both 32-bit (x86) and 64-bit (x64) Visual C++ Redistributable packages; 3) Run the application as Administrator; 4) Run 'sfc /scannow' in admin command prompt to replace damaged system DLLs; 5) Reinstall the affected program cleanly.

question: How do I clear application cache to resolve glitches and corrupted app states?
alternatives: How to clear app cache in Windows?
Clear temporary files for a specific program
Reset an application without reinstalling
Clear Windows Store app cache wsreset
answer: To clear app cache: 1) For Microsoft Store apps: go to Settings > Apps > Installed apps, click the three dots on the app > Advanced options > click 'Reset' or 'Repair'; 2) To reset the Microsoft Store itself, run 'wsreset.exe' in the Run dialog (Win + R); 3) For desktop programs (like Spotify, Discord, Slack): close the app, open Run (Win + R), type '%AppData%', locate the app folder, and delete the 'Cache' subfolder inside.

question: How do I know if an email is a phishing scam?
alternatives: How to spot a phishing email?

Is this suspicious email real or fake?
How to recognize phishing attacks?
answer: Key indicators of a phishing email: 1) Inconsistent sender address: the display name says 'PayPal' or 'Bank', but the actual address domain is random (e.g. support@payp-security-alert.xyz); 2) Artificial urgency, threatening account suspension or legal action if you don't act immediately; 3) Generic greetings like 'Dear Customer'; 4) Suspicious links: hover over links without clicking to preview the destination URL; 5) Unsolicited attachments (.zip, .html, .exe, or password-protected files).

question: Is Windows Defender / Windows Security enough protection against malware?
alternatives: Do I need third-party antivirus with Windows Defender?
Is built-in Windows antivirus good enough?
Should I buy Norton, McAfee, or keep Windows Defender?
How secure is Windows Security in Windows 11?
answer: For most everyday users, built-in Windows Security (Windows Defender) provides excellent, lightweight protection. It offers real-time antivirus scanning, cloud-delivered malware definitions, ransomware file protection, and a firewall without the performance bloat or aggressive upselling of legacy third-party antivirus suites. Combined with basic safe computing habits (ad-blocker like uBlock Origin, updated browser, not opening sketchy downloads), it is thoroughly sufficient.

question: How do I run a full offline malware scan using Microsoft Defender?

question: What is ransomware and how can I protect my personal files against it?

question: What is the difference between Sleep, Hibernate, and Shut Down?
alternatives: Sleep vs Hibernate vs Shut Down explained
Should I shut down or sleep my laptop?
Difference between hibernate and sleep in Windows
Is it bad to leave PC in sleep mode?
answer: Here is the distinction: 1) Sleep: puts your PC into a low-power state and keeps open documents and apps in RAM for instant wake-up in seconds (uses a small trickle of battery); 2) Hibernate: saves your open session to the SSD/hard drive (hiberfil.sys) and powers down completely (zero battery usage, resumes session on boot); 3) Shut Down: closes all programs, kernel sessions, and powers off completely, ensuring fresh system startup.

question: How do I check my computer's hardware specifications (CPU, RAM, GPU, SSD)?

question: How do I customize and manage notifications in Windows to avoid distractions?

question: How do I fix a USB flash drive or external hard drive not showing up in File Explorer?

question: How do I clear printer queue when a document is stuck printing?

question: Why is my laptop battery draining so fast and how can I generate a battery health report?

question: How do I fix screen flickering, flashing, or horizontal lines on my computer monitor?

question: Why does my computer turn on and then turn off immediately after a few seconds?
alternatives: PC turns on then immediately shuts down

PC boot loop shuts down in 5 seconds

computer chalu hoke turant band ho raha hai
answer: If a computer powers off immediately after starting: 1) Thermal protection cutoff: the CPU heatsink or thermal paste may have detached, causing thermal shutdown within seconds to prevent CPU destruction; 2) Faulty Power Supply Unit (PSU): an aging power supply may trip when power rails spike on boot; 3) RAM short: reseat memory sticks one by one; 4) Disconnect all external USB peripherals to eliminate short circuits on USB headers; 5) Clear CMOS by removing the motherboard coin-cell battery for 5 minutes.

question: Why does my laptop charger or power adapter get extremely hot when charging?
alternatives: Laptop power brick burning hot

Laptop charger feels too hot to touch
answer: It is normal for power adapters to get warm (up to 45-50°C) during fast-charging, but extreme burning heat indicates poor heat dissipation or electrical resistance: 1) Keep the charger in a well-ventilated space on a hard floor or desk—never under blankets, pillows, or inside bags; 2) Inspect the cable and barrel/USB-C connector for fraying, bends, or loose contacts; 3) Ensure the adapter wattage matches your laptop manufacturer's exact specifications; 4) If the plastic casing smells burnt or is warping, disconnect immediately and replace it.

question: How do I fix my laptop microphone not working or not picking up my voice?

question: Why is there no sound through HDMI on my TV or external monitor?

question: How do I fix a Wi-Fi connection that says 'Action needed' and open captive portal login?

question: How do I view saved Wi-Fi passwords for connected networks on Windows?

answer: To view your Wi-Fi password: 1) Settings method: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi > click on your connected Wi-Fi network properties, scroll down and click 'View Wi-Fi security key'; 2) Command Prompt method (works for any previously saved network): Open Command Prompt, run 'netsh wlan show profile name="YourNetworkName" key=clear', and locate the 'Key Content' field under Security Settings to view the plain-text password.

question: How do I fix 'Unidentified Network - No Internet' on Ethernet or LAN cable?

question: How do I resolve the 'DNS Server Not Responding' error in Windows?
alternatives: DNS server is not responding error
How to fix DNS server errors?
Websites won't open DNS server not responding
Troubleshoot DNS failure Windows
answer: To fix 'DNS Server Not Responding': 1) Flush DNS cache: open Command Prompt as Administrator and run 'ipconfig /flushdns', 'ipconfig /registerdns', and 'netsh winsock reset'; 2) Switch to public reliable DNS: go to Network Settings > Wi-Fi/Ethernet > Hardware Properties > DNS > Edit, and enter Google DNS (8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4) or Cloudflare (1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1); 3) Restart your router; 4) Temporarily disable third-party antivirus firewall which might be blocking port 53 DNS queries.

question: How do I remove a PIN and sign in with a traditional password in Windows?

question: What should I do if Windows shows 'We can't sign in to your account' temporary profile error?

We can't sign in to your account error
Corrupted user profile in Windows

answer: This happens when Windows fails to read your user registry hive and loads a temporary profile: 1) DO NOT save new files on the desktop, as temporary profiles are deleted upon logout; 2) Restart your PC 2-3 times (often resolves temporary file locks); 3) In Registry Editor (regedit.exe as Admin), navigate to: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList; 4) Check for a profile folder ending in '.bak'. Delete the duplicate non-bak entry, and rename the '.bak' folder by removing the '.bak' extension; 5) Reboot.

question: How do I find my BitLocker recovery key and manage drive encryption?

question: How do I remove 'The disk is write-protected' error on a USB flash drive or SD card?

answer: To clear write protection on a USB drive: 1) Check physical lock switch: inspect the side of SD cards or USB sticks for a physical sliding 'Lock' switch and slide it forward; 2) Clear read-only attributes via Diskpart: open Command Prompt as Admin, type 'diskpart' > 'list disk' > 'select disk X' (where X is your USB number) > 'attributes disk clear readonly' > 'exit'; 3) Check Registry: in regedit, navigate to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\StorageDevicePolicies, and change 'WriteProtect' to 0.

question: How do I identify and delete duplicate files safely to free up disk space?

answer: To remove duplicate files safely: 1) Use reputable open-source or free dedicated tools such as 'Czkawka' or 'Duplicate Cleaner Free'; 2) Never blindly scan the 'C:\Windows' or 'C:\Program Files' directories—only scan your personal folders (Downloads, Documents, Pictures); 3) Compare by SHA-256 or MD5 hash rather than file name alone to ensure files are truly identical; 4) Review files before confirming deletion.

question: How do I permanently delete sensitive files so they cannot be recovered by forensic software?

Secure file deletion so recuva can't restore
Wipe sensitive documents permanently

answer: Standard Recycle Bin deletion only unlinks file references; the raw bytes remain until overwritten. To shred data permanently: 1) Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin; 2) Wipe residual free space using the built-in Windows cipher command: open Command Prompt as Admin and type 'cipher /w:C:' to write 0s, 1s, and random bytes over deleted sectors; 3) For individual file shredding, use trusted utilities like Eraser (eraser.heidi.ie) using DoD 5220.22-M sanitization standards.

question: Why does my screen say 'Activate Windows - Go to Settings to activate Windows' and how do I fix it?

question: How do I enable Hardware Virtualization (VT-x / AMD-V) in BIOS for WSL, Hyper-V, and emulators?

question: How do I fix Windows time and date not synchronizing or constantly showing the wrong time?

question: How do I fix 'Display driver stopped responding and has recovered' graphics crash?

question: How do I fix Discord, Slack, or game audio sounding robotic, distorted, or cutting out?

question: How do I check if my computer is being remotely controlled or monitored by unauthorized users?

question: What immediate steps should I take if I accidentally downloaded or opened a suspicious file?
